target: Στο τέλος δεν θέλαμε να φύγουμε.
english: In the end we did not want to leave.
tip: δεν θέλαμε (den thélame) is imperfect because wanting is a state, not an event – the not-wanting-to-leave lasted the whole end of the trip.

target: Το κράνος είναι υποχρεωτικό και για τους δύο.
english: The helmet is mandatory for both riders.
tip: τους δύο (tus dío) with the article means 'the two' = both. Bare δύο (dío) just counts; και για τους δύο (ke ya tus dío) = for both of them.

target: Ο δρόμος ήταν χωματόδρομος και οδηγούσαμε αργά.
english: The road was a dirt road and we were driving slowly.
tip: Both verbs are imperfect – ήταν (ítan) and οδηγούσαμε (odigúsame) – pure scene-setting: the road stayed dirt, the driving stayed slow, nothing 'happens' yet.

target: Το μηχανάκι έμεινε από βενζίνη στην ανηφόρα.
english: The moped ran out of petrol on the uphill.
tip: μένω από (méno apó) is literally 'be left from' = to run out of: έμεινε από βενζίνη (émine apó venzíni) = it ran out of petrol.

target: Γεμίσαμε το ντεπόζιτο πριν φύγουμε.
english: We filled the tank before we left.
tip: πριν + verb = before doing: πριν φύγουμε (prin fígume) = before we left.

target: Μην οδηγείς χωρίς κράνος στο νησί.
english: Do not ride without a helmet on the island.
tip: Commands negate with μη(ν) (min), not δεν (den): μην οδηγείς (min odiyís) = don't ride. δεν (den) states facts; μη(ν) (min) forbids.

target: Κάθε πρωί κολυμπούσαμε πριν από το πρωινό.
english: Every morning we swam before breakfast.
tip: Imperfect for habits: κολυμπούσαμε (kolimboúsame) = we would swim.

target: Ένα βράδυ φάγαμε ψάρι δίπλα στη θάλασσα.
english: One evening we ate fish by the sea.
tip: ένα βράδυ (éna vrádi) + aorist pins one specific evening, one finished event: φάγαμε (fágame) = we ate, that night and done.

target: Ενώ τρώγαμε, άρχισε δυνατή βροχή.
english: While we were eating, heavy rain started.
tip: ενώ + imperfect = while: ενώ τρώγαμε (enó trógame) = while we were eating.

target: Ξαφνικά νύχτωσε και γυρίσαμε γρήγορα.
english: Suddenly night fell and we went back quickly.
tip: ξαφνικά (xafniká) = suddenly pairs with the aorist: νύχτωσε (níchtose) = night fell, one sharp event. Sudden things take the one-shot past tense.

target: Περπατούσαμε στο λιμάνι όταν είδαμε τα δελφίνια.
english: We were walking at the harbor when we saw the dolphins.
tip: The classic pair: imperfect περπατούσαμε (perpatúsame) = we were walking, the backdrop; aorist είδαμε (ídame) = we saw, the event that cuts in.

target: Το βράδυ η γιαγιά έλεγε ιστορίες για το χωριό.
english: In the evening grandma would tell stories about the village.
tip: έλεγε (éleye) is imperfect for a habit: grandma told stories evening after evening. One single telling would be είπε (ípe).

target: Γνωρίσαμε ένα ζευγάρι από τη Θεσσαλονίκη.
english: We met a couple from Thessaloniki.
tip: γνωρίζω (gnorízo) = to know, but its one-shot past means met for the first time: γνωρίσαμε (gnorísame) = we met. The knowing began at one moment.

target: Ένα απόγευμα με πήρε ο ύπνος στην παραλία!
english: One afternoon I fell asleep on the beach!
tip: με πήρε ο ύπνος (me píre o ípnos) is literally 'sleep took me' = I dozed off. Sleep is the doer in Greek; you're just the one it grabs.

target: Ένα βράδυ χορεύαμε μέχρι τα ξημερώματα.
english: One night we danced until dawn.
tip: χορεύαμε (chorévame) is imperfect even with ένα βράδυ (éna vrádi) – the point is that the dancing went on for hours, and duration beats the one-night frame.

target: Αξίζει να πας οπωσδήποτε στη Μήλο.
english: It is definitely worth going to Milos.
tip: αξίζει να (axízi na) + verb = it's worth ...ing: αξίζει να πας (axízi na pas) = it's worth going – no 'it' subject needed.

target: Μην πας τον Αύγουστο, έχει πολύ κόσμο.
english: Do not go in August, it is very crowded.
tip: έχει κόσμο (échi kósmo) is literally 'it has people' = it's crowded. Impersonal έχει covers conditions too: έχει ζέστη (échi zésti) = it's hot.

target: Η διαδρομή με το καραβάκι αξίζει τα λεφτά της.
english: The ride on the little boat is worth the money.
tip: -άκι makes things little: το καραβάκι (karaváki) = the little boat.

target: Για το ηλιοβασίλεμα πήγαινε τουλάχιστον μία ώρα νωρίτερα.
english: For the sunset, go at least an hour earlier.
tip: Adverbs compare with -τερα: νωρίς (norís = early) becomes νωρίτερα (norítera = earlier) – no extra word for 'more' needed.

target: Μη χάσεις τη βόλτα στα παλιά σοκάκια.
english: Do not miss the walk in the old alleys.
tip: One verb covers both: χάνω (cháno) is 'lose' and 'miss' – μη χάσεις τη βόλτα (mi chásis ti vólta) = don't miss the walk.

target: Του χρόνου θέλουμε να πάμε σε άλλο νησί.
english: Next year we want to go to another island.
tip: του χρόνου (tu chrónu) = next year — literally 'of the year'.

target: Μαζεύω λεφτά για το επόμενο ταξίδι.
english: I am saving money for the next trip.
tip: μαζεύω λεφτά (mazévo leftá) = I save money — literally 'gather'.

target: Περάσαμε τέλεια, δεν θέλαμε να γυρίσουμε.
english: We had a great time, we did not want to come back.
tip: Time is passed, not had: περάσαμε τέλεια (perásame télia) is literally 'we passed perfectly' – Greek's way of saying we had a great time.

target: Ψάχνω δουλειά εδώ και τρεις μήνες.
english: I've been looking for a job for three months.
tip: εδώ και τρεις μήνες (edó ke tris mínes) = literally 'here and three months'. With plain present ψάχνω (psáchno) it means 'I've been looking for three months now'.

target: Μου είπαν ότι θα με πάρουν τηλέφωνο.
english: They told me they'd call me.
tip: The 'me' goes before the verb: θα με πάρουν (tha me pároun) = literally 'they'll me take'. In statements, short object pronouns slot in front of the verb.

target: Δεν με πήραν ποτέ τηλέφωνο τελικά.
english: In the end they never called me.
tip: Stacking negatives is correct Greek: δεν με πήραν ποτέ (den me píran poté) = literally 'they didn't take me never' – that's the standard way to say 'never'.

target: Θα ξαναπάρω την εταιρεία αύριο το πρωί.
english: I'll call the company back tomorrow morning.
tip: 'Call back' is 'call again': ξανα- (xana = again) glues onto the verb – θα ξαναπάρω (tha xanapáro) = I'll call again. Never παίρνω πίσω (pérno píso = take back).

target: Έκανα αίτηση για τρεις διαφορετικές θέσεις.
english: I applied for three different positions.
tip: You 'make an application': έκανα αίτηση (ékana aítisi) = I applied. The lookalike εφαρμόζω (efarmózo) means implement, not apply for a job.

target: Ελπίζω να βρω κάτι σχετικό με τις σπουδές μου.
english: I hope to find something related to my studies.
tip: Where English uses 'to', Greek links verbs with να: ελπίζω να βρω (elpízo na vro) = I hope to find – there's no plain infinitive to fall back on.

target: Μου είπαν να περάσω για μια κουβέντα.
english: They told me to drop by for a chat.
tip: Dropping by is 'passing': να περάσω για μια κουβέντα (na peráso ya mia kouvénda) = literally 'to pass by for a chat' – περνάω (pernáo) covers casual visits.
